title: Orchestrated cohort upgrades and safety-matrix for adaptive rollouts
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Implement a repeatable, observable, and automatable pipeline for phased upgrades that targets small cohorts first, warms caches, validates inference quality, and enforces safety gates with automated rollback. This ticket builds an orchestrator that combines cohort-aware traffic routing, synthetic canary traffic, golden-prompt evaluation, and a safety-matrix engine that codifies multi-signal gate rules (latency, error-rate, correctness).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Orchestrator can run a staged rollout: shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with configurable hold windows.
2) Safety matrix evaluates signals (p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, correctness delta on golden prompts) and emits PASS/WARN/FAIL per cohort.
3) Automated rollback triggers when FAIL conditions persist for configured window.
4) Cohort warming: KV cache pre-warm via synthetic prefix traffic prior to ramp.
5) Runbook and automated playbook produce reproducible post-rollback artifact links.
design_decisions: Use cohort IDs instead of pure percent-of-traffic to allow sticky routing for long-lived sessions and KV warmup.
Combine absolute and relative thresholds: absolute latency spike (p95 + 200ms) OR relative error increase (>3x baseline) to trigger FAIL — prevents minor noise causing rollbacks.
Implement a cooldown doubling strategy: if a WARN is observed at X% traffic, pause and extend the hold window; on repeated WARNs double backoff and optionally reduce next ramp step.
Expose 'morph' flag that migrates cohorts gradually by moving cohort membership (useful for nomadic clients tied to specific L7 proxies).
safety_matrix: Signals considered: p50_latency, p95_latency, 5xx_rate, client_error_rate, golden_prompt_failure_rate, kv-warmness. FAIL if any of: p95 >= baseline_p95 + 200ms for 5m, OR 5xx_rate >= 0.5% absolute AND >=3x baseline for 3m, OR golden_prompt_failure_rate increase >= 5% absolute. WARN for smaller deviations. PASS otherwise.

next_steps: 1) Finish wiring cohort-level customer_impact metadata into Console. 2) Expand golden prompt set by +300 examples covering embeddings/regression patterns. 3) Run one staged rollout against a non-prod region and record automated rollback behavior. 4) Draft postmortem template for rollbacks triggered by safety matrix.
notes_for_reviewers: Key tradeoffs: conservative thresholds reduce risk of regressions but increase roll-out time. We recommend an initial conservative default (1% -> 5% -> 25%) and enable product teams to opt into faster ramps with higher monitoring. Please review safety thresholds and the cooldown strategy.
estimated_risks: False positives in safety triggers (noisy metrics), KV warmup insufficiency, and corner-case client routing for long-lived sessions. Mitigations: increase aggregation windows, include relative thresholds, and use cohort-sticky routing.
implementation_notes: Orchestrator will be implemented as a control-plane microservice with idempotent operations, storing cohort state in Consul and emitting events to the rollout-audit Kafka topic. Rollback will call the stable routing API and create an incident via PagerDuty with automatic context payload.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for threshold evaluation. 2) Simulation harness run with randomized failure injection. 3) End-to-end rehearsal in staging region: shadow -> 1% -> 5% and validate no unintended regressions. 4) Chaos test that injects delayed KV responses to ensure rollback triggers.
estimated_rollback_criteria: FAIL persists for >=3 continuous minutes OR golden_prompt_failure_rate delta >= 5% for 10m. On rollback, reroute affected cohorts to last stable and spawn regression job to collect evidence.
legal_compliance_notes: No PII in synthetic canary traffic. Audit events retained for 90 days by default; enterprise tenants can request extended retention via Private deployment settings.
